answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a month before it earns voting weight, then cap weight by the square root of the stake. Spinning up thousands of Sybils no longer multiplies influence: the attacker must buy and immobilize enough tokens, paying opportunity cost and risking slashing for proven fraud. A summit can set the lock period; the horizon measures how long capital stays trapped, while a trellis of attestations links identities to their stake history.
